summary.oneLiner: CONCOR delivered record FY26 throughput of **5.58 mn TEUs (+9.6% YoY)** and crossed **INR6,000 cr EXIM revenue for the first time**, yet PAT fell ~4.5% as the domestic segment was crushed by collapse of Gunny-Bales (jute supply disruption from neighbouring country) and Morbi tiles (gas shortage) traffic, forcing costly empty running. The big structural catalyst is **WDFC-to-JNPT connectivity commissioned 1-Jun-2026**, enabling NCR↔JNPT double-stack trains; mgmt expects JNPT rail coefficient to rise from 15.1% → 18-19% in FY27 and 30-35% over 3 years. FY27 guidance: EXIM +8%, Domestic +15%, overall **+9.5% handling volume**, EBITDA held at **24-25%**. New optionality from tank-container bulk cement, BCSL shipping line (30% stake), and PSA dedicated JNPA service.

thesis (in one paragraph): CONCOR delivered record FY26 throughput of **5.58 mn TEUs (+9.6% YoY)** and crossed **INR6,000 cr EXIM revenue for the first time**, yet PAT fell ~4.5% as the domestic segment was crushed by collapse of Gunny-Bales (jute supply disruption from neighbouring country) and Morbi tiles (gas shortage) traffic, forcing costly empty running. FY27 guidance: EXIM +8%, Domestic +15%, overall **+9.5% handling volume**, EBITDA held at **24-25%**. New optionality from tank-container bulk cement, BCSL shipping line (30% stake), and PSA dedicated JNPA service.

guidance (critical):
- **Volume growth FY27 (handling): EXIM +8%, Domestic +15%, Overall +9.5%** — mgmt explicitly "conservative" given geopolitics; midyear review possible.
- **Margin: EBITDA held 24-25%** (vs 24.33% FY26).
- **DFC ramp:** WDFC↔JNPT commissioned 1-Jun-2026; double-stack NCR→JNPT from June. JNPT rail coefficient 15.1% → **18-19% (maybe 20-21%) in FY27**, → **30-35% in 3 years**.
- **Capex FY27: INR945 cr approved** by Board (vs INR1,085.2 cr spent FY26 — one of highest ever); likely raised at midyear review toward ~INR1,000 cr+.
- No long-term guidance given (declined beyond FY27 due to uncertainty).
- Bulk cement in tank containers: target **at least 1 mn tons in FY27**.
volumes / pipeline:
- FY26 handling 5.58 mn TEUs (EXIM 4.21 mn). Domestic does 14-15 mn tons loading/yr.
- Double-stack rakes: 6,302 → 6,396 (+1.5%); high-speed rakes +43 to 423; new containers +4,729 to fleet of 57,746 owned; tank containers fleet 500 now, +200/month; Board approved +2,000 (on top of earlier 1,000) tank containers.
- DPD volumes +38% after liberalized DPD/cabotage policy. Reefer exports +17%.
- New terminals commissioned: Mandalgarh, Kadakola (nr Mysuru), Jajpur, Paradip; double-stack at Salawas (nr Jodhpur) & Chharodi (nr Ahmedabad, on DFC).
- Nepal traffic: Birgunj + new Raxaul point; Biratnagar to start.
- Pending order pipeline: GAIL & Petronet (bulk volumes), food-grain bulk loading trials successful, gunny-bales revival, assured-transit-time trains (Tughlakabad→Shalimar live).
segment (exim / domestic):
- **EXIM:** Star performer — >INR6,000 cr revenue (record), 4.21 mn TEUs (record), handling +8%. Export growth +3% (auto parts +17%, buffalo meat +19%, aluminium ingots +22%); imports +5.8% (auto parts +38%, solar panel parts +92%, polymer +23%). Port import growth: JNPT +12%, Mundra +8.8%, Chennai +14%, Vizag +28%. Hurt by West Asia crisis (Middle East movement stopped; ~700 containers had gone to ME under own BL).
- **Domestic:** Hammered — Q4 revenue −4%, segment EBIT margin just 0.2%. Causes: Gunny-Bales collapse (jute supply disruption) → empty back-haul from Eastern India; Morbi tiles factories shut (no gas); tank-container shortage. Below 50% of normal on gunny/Morbi but reviving. New driver = bulk cement in tank containers.
- **Market share (FY26):** EXIM 53.9% (vs 55.2%); Domestic 55.9% (vs 57.6%); Overall 54.5% (vs 55.9%) — marginal drop, partly by choice (avoided low-margin business). Port rail coefficients/share: JNPT 15.12% coeff / 60% share; Mundra 24.6% / 35.4%; Pipavav 57.5% / 48.3%.
growth / optionality:
- **WDFC**: NCR↔JNPT double-stack from 1-Jun-2026 — core catalyst; tariff "tinkering" to share upper-deck haulage savings (50% haulage on upper deck) with customers to pull road→rail light cargo.
- **PSA agreement (JNPA)**: dedicated JNPA↔CONCOR ICD service; unique customs permission to carry domestic + cabotage + EXIM on same double-stack train from PSA's DFC-compliant yard. Other JNPT terminals now approaching CONCOR for similar deals.
- **BCSL (Bharat Container Shipping Line)**: 30% stake; partners SCI (30%), JNPT/Chennai/Tuticorin ports, Sagarmala Dev Fund. Target top-10 global shipping line by 2047 (Amrit Kaal vision). Capex confidential (going to Cabinet); PIB release cited INR59,000 cr Atmanirbhar outlay (mgmt declined to confirm CONCOR share).
- **Tank containers / bulk cement** (domestic), **food-grain bulk** trials, **Aushadhi Express** (Hyderabad ICD→JNPT pharma, with Maersk), Nepal expansion, shipping to Far East started.
margins & cost:
- EBITDA 24.33% (FY26) vs 24.9% (FY25) — resilient; guided 24-25%.
- Rail freight margin 27.16% (+1.51pp); overall operating margin 30.89% (+0.9pp).
- Empty-running reduction overall −10.5% (EXIM −27%, domestic ~−4%) aided bottom line, but Q4 domestic empties +11.3% YoY hit segment margin to 0.2%.
- Other expenses up to INR358 cr (FY); Q4 ~INR120 cr vs ~INR80 cr normal — maintenance/AMC (new DR site), CSR — flagged recurring, not one-off.
- DFC haulage = same rate as IR; savings only via 50% upper-deck haulage on double stack. No haulage hike currently planned by IR.
capex: - FY26 capex **INR1,085.20 cr** (one of highest ever). FY27 approved **INR945 cr**, likely raised at midyear toward FY26 level (~INR1,000 cr/yr is the norm). Spend on rakes, containers, terminals, tank containers, green logistics (230 LNG trucks, 5 electric RSTs, 2 EVs on trial). Long-term 10 mn TEU target (~FY29-30) reaffirmed in spirit; "future ready" philosophy.
capital allocation (psu dividend): - Total FY26 dividend **INR8.6/share** (172% of INR5 par); Q4 interim INR1/sh. Debt-free; disciplined capex ~INR1,000 cr/yr funded internally. BCSL equity investment (quantum confidential, Cabinet-bound).
risks:
- West Asia / Middle East conflict halting ME container movement; geopolitical & tariff (US up to 50%) hits to textiles/marine exports.
- Domestic concentration risk: gunny-bales (jute supply) & Morbi tiles (gas) — both below 50% of normal.
- Lead-distance erosion compressing revenue conversion (EXIM lead −3 km).
- Market-share slippage (overall 55.9%→54.5%).
- Recurring other-expense uplift (~+1.5pp EBITDA drag risk if not normalized).
- Tank-container ecosystem maturity / supply dependency.
- April FY27 start weak (only May picked up).
management tone: Confident on EXIM record and WDFC catalyst; candid and specific on domestic pain (gunny/Morbi/empty-running) with granular numbers. Deliberately conservative on guidance and refused long-term forecast. Tight-lipped on BCSL economics, PSA contract terms, Mundra-vs-JNPT cargo shift, and current-quarter empty-running specifics. Strong PSU/governance-pride framing in closing.
non-obvious insights:
- Originating ≈ 65-70% of handling; earnings = f(weight × lead) — so volume headlines overstate revenue; lead compression is the silent margin/revenue drag.
- Nagpur/Hyderabad/Bangalore EXIM cargo to JNPT is NOT on WDFC → cannot double-stack → DFC upside is concentrated in NCR & Gujarat corridors; the path to 30% JNPT coefficient also relies on slow road→rail on non-DFC routes.
- Q4 domestic empty-running spiked +11.3% YoY even though FY empties fell 3.8% — the damage was concentrated and quarter-specific.
- "Other expenses" structurally stepped up (DR site AMC + CSR) — recurring ~+1.5pp cost, not a one-off to add back.
- PSA deal's real edge = single train carrying domestic + cabotage + EXIM (special customs permission, open to all) — a template now sought by rival JNPT terminals.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- WDFC commissioning → CONCOR (double-stack economics), DFCCIL; ICD/terminal ecosystem.
- Road→rail shift on diesel-driven freight inflation → rail CTOs (CONCOR primary).
- BCSL container-line build-out → CONCOR, SCI, JNPT/Chennai/Tuticorin ports, tank/box & ship suppliers.
- Tank-container bulk cement → cement makers' logistics, tank-container vendors (3 domestic vendors emerging).
- ✅/⭐ specific listed-beneficiary picks: none flagged (PSU JV partners SCI, port trusts not separately actionable here).

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
